title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page belongs to the continuation of 'La Longue Marche', roughly the 1981 programme on the anabelian and Teichmüller tower. The previous page fixed the setting. For a curve M of type (g,ν) over a field k, π = π1(M,a) is a profinite group with an 'L-structure', meaning the distinguished inertia or 'lacet' conjugacy classes around the ν punctures. Over a general k (most interesting: k finitely generated over Q) one has the exact sequence (12): 1 → π1(M_kbar) → π1(M) → Gal(kbar/k) → 1. This makes π a 'Π-groupe', an extension of a Galois-type group by a geometric profinite L-group of type (g,ν).

This page says the case of most interest is the 'universal' one. There the base is not Spec k but the modular stacks ('multiplicités modulaires') M_{g,ν}. The next page writes the corresponding sequence (13): 1 → Π^_{g,ν} → π1(universal curve over M_{g,ν,Q}) → π1(M_{g,ν,Q}) → 1.

The bracketed remark generalizes this. Take any discrete L-group π0 as the reference group, not necessarily the surface group of type (g,ν); possibly it has torsion, i.e. is an orbifold or Fuchsian-type group. Grothendieck says one should be able to define a modular stack over Q, and even over Z, classifying relative 'multiplicities' (stacky curves) whose geometric fundamental L-group is of type π0.

He then names the conceptual obstacle. A modular stack such as M_{g,ν} is a fibered category in groupoids over (Sch), namely the category of relative curves of type (g,ν). The objects to be classified here are themselves relative multiplicities, i.e. stacks over the base S. These form a 2-category fibered in groupoids over (Sch): objects are stacks, 1-morphisms are equivalences, 2-morphisms are natural isomorphisms. So the 'moduli' object is a priori a 2-stack, not a stack.

Purpose: to place the anabelian Galois–Teichmüller theory in a setting uniform over all 'types' π0, including orbifold types, over arithmetic bases. This is the stack-theoretic foundation for the Π-groupe formalism developed on the next pages.
errors: No outright error. One nuance: the 2-categorical nature is genuine only when the classified multiplicities have nontrivial generic stabilizer, i.e. are gerbes over curves, which happens when π0 has a nontrivial finite normal subgroup. If generic stabilizers are trivial, 2-automorphisms of 1-morphisms are trivial and the 2-category is equivalent to a 1-category, i.e. an ordinary stack. This is the mechanism later used for twisted curves by Abramovich–Vistoli and Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli. So the 'difficulty' is avoidable for orbifold curves with trivial generic stabilizer.

The claim 'even over Z' hides wild phenomena when residue characteristics divide torsion orders in π0. The modern fix needs tame stacks (Abramovich–Olsson–Vistoli) or restriction to Z[1/N]; Grothendieck does not address this.

ideas.what: Universal case: work over the moduli stack M_{g,ν} as base rather than Spec k; the profinite π1 of the universal curve is a Π-group.
ideas.modern_name: Universal monodromy / Teichmüller-modular tower, geometric vs arithmetic fundamental group of M_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984); developed by Ihara, Nakamura, Matsumoto and others
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme; La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: For an arbitrary discrete L-group π0 (reference 'type', possibly with torsion), a modular stack over Q or Z classifying relative multiplicities (stacky curves) of type π0.
ideas.modern_name: Moduli of orbifold or stacky curves of given signature; twisted curves; tame stacky curves
ideas.where_published: Esquisse discusses multiplicities modulaires and orbifold types loosely; this explicit formulation is not known to me in published texts

ideas.what: Moduli of stacks is naturally a 2-category fibered in groupoids over (Sch), i.e. a 2-stack, not a stack.
ideas.modern_name: Moduli 2-stacks / higher stacks; truncation to 1-stacks when generic stabilizer is trivial
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; Breen (1994), Hirschowitz–Simpson, Toën–Vezzosi; ACV for the truncation criterion
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983) treats n-stacks in general; this specific moduli-of-multiplicities remark predates it

missed.claim: Around 1981, before Pursuing Stacks, Grothendieck explicitly notes that classifying stacky curves (multiplicities) of a given discrete fundamental-group type over Z leads to a 2-stack. He thus ties anabelian geometry with orbifold types to higher stacks. This is an early documented motivation for higher stacks coming from moduli of orbicurves.
missed.quote: les multiplicités relatives correspondantes à un "type" π0-donné forment (en groupoïdes) une 2-catégorie fibrée sur (Sch), et pas seulement une catégorie fibrée...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically documents an origin of Grothendieck's interest in 2-/n-stacks within anabelian geometry. Mathematically, moduli of gerby orbicurves with nontrivial generic stabilizer are genuine 2-stacks. Galois actions on their fundamental groups (Π-groups of gerbe type) are little studied.

missed.claim: A programme of modular multiplicities over Z for every discrete L-type π0, including types with torsion, as bases for universal Π-groups. It is only partially realized: twisted or tame stacky curves cover trivial-generic-stabilizer types, and the arithmetic over Z at primes dividing torsion orders remains delicate.
missed.quote: on doit pouvoir introduire une multiplicité modulaire correspondante sur Q, et même sur Z.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory indexed by general orbifold types over Z, including the 2-stack case, is not systematically developed in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The ideas, moduli of orbicurves and moduli of stacks being 2-stacks, are now standard or folklore. However, this is an early explicit appearance (around 1981, pre-Pursuing Stacks) of 2-stacks arising naturally in Grothendieck's anabelian programme, which is of historical interest. No finished new result.
